title.narrative: Australia's Budget Support Program for Samoa

description.narrative: Budget Support provides Samoa with budget certainty and control to deliver on its own priorities. Australia’s 2022 Assessment of National Systems update affirmed that Samoa’s systems are robust and there is a demonstrable commitment to continual improvement and lowering residual fiduciary risks. In partnership with New Zealand, the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank and the European Union, this investment utilizes Samoa's Joint Policy Action Matrix (JPAM) mechanism to facilitate budget support payments aligned with the delivery of priority policy reforms agreed with Samoa. The Tautai program supports implementation through technical and other wrap-around assistance.

GOVERNMENT OF SAMOA - MINISTRY OF FINANCE

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia provided technical assistance, incentivised through general budget support, to support the Samoa Ministry of Commerce Industry and Labour to advance a new and improved Foreign Investment Amendment Act and associated regulations. The Amendment outlines provisions for investor rights, market access and contains other provisions to promote additional investment and protect Samoan sovereignty in line with international best practice. The Amendment’s approval as a trigger for a budget support disbursement further incentivised these important changes that help to promote Samoan growth and prosperity. Through Tautai – Governance for Economic Growth, Australian funded advisers supported drafting of the legislation. ‍ The Foreign Investment Amendment Bill is pending the new Parliament session and Australia stands ready to support Samoa implement their new investment framework.

Australia’s Bilateral General Budget Support Investment implemented through Samoa’s multi-donor Joint Policy Action Matrix (JPAM) contributed to the incentivisation of key reforms for two government ministries in Samoa, to strengthen accountability and inclusion. Through JPAM, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour was supported to operationalise the Labour Employment Relations Amendment Act 2023, which sought to align Samoa’s labour laws with international labour standards and improve clarity on employment terms and conditions and grievances processes. This support enabled the Samoan government to complete the ratification of ILO Conventions 187 and 190 on 31 May 2024. The Central Bank of Samoa was supported through JPAM to develop the second National Financial Inclusion Strategy for Samoa. A key focus of this Strategy is to increase the number of adults having access and using formal financial services to 40,000 by 2025-2026, with at least 50% being women.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia’s Bilateral General Budget Support Investment, implemented through Samoa’s multi-donor Joint Policy Action Matrix (JPAM), contributed to the incentivization of continued Public Financial Management reforms in Samoa. The reforms completed in the reporting period include organizational changes in the Ministry of Finance with the establishment of two new divisions, Debt Management and Fixed Asset Management, to further strengthen Samoa’s national systems. The Debt Management Division will help strengthen Samoa’s capacity for prudent and sustainable debt management. The Fixed Asset Management Division will help socialize Samoa’s new Fixed Asset Management Policy Framework across government ministries. The Fixed Asset Management Policy includes financial protection perspectives, in addition to infrastructure for management of all government fixed assets. The two new Divisions came into effect on 1 July 2024.

Australia’s Budget Support continued to contribute to strengthened accountability and inclusion in Samoa through the Joint Policy Action Matrix – a suite of policy actions mutually agreed between Samoa and development partners. Wrap around support provided by Tautai – Governance for Economic Growth contributed to Samoa’s continuing strong economic conditions, enabling Australia to continue, and expand, its budget support program. ‍ Such conditions included heightened risk management practices with a whole-of-government scope (all ministries and public bodies), being implemented with Tautai support. The risk management framework standardises risk policy, integrates procedures for risk assessment and mitigation into planning and monitoring systems, and provides a suite of tools (e.g. risk registers). ‍ Additionally, capability uplift for internal auditors focused on IT responds to increasing cyber security threats, and the Samoa Audit Office completed a cold review of compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards for all public bodies. Both activities supported by Australian funded advisers.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia’s Budget Support continued to incentivise Public Financial Management reforms in Samoa through the Joint Policy Action Matrix (JPAM) and wrap around support provided through Tautai – Governance for Economic Growth. ‍ The Ministry of Finance’s capacity to advise Cabinet on investment decisions has improved through Australian funded advisers who strengthened staff skills in the economic policy and planning division and updated manuals framing sector-wide planning and investment processes. This included integrating climate, gender equality, disability and social inclusion in sector planning and investment project decision making. ‍ Australia also funded an ICT industry specialist to assist the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology to review and assess Government’s connectivity service fees and cost structures, to provide comparative analysis and recommendations. The assessment provides baseline data for the World Bank funded (US35m) Digitally Connected and Resilient Samoa Project which aims to support the establishment of climate and disaster resilient digital connectivity.

Australia’s bilateral general budget support investment implemented through Samoa’s multi-donor Joint Policy Action Matrix, contributed to the incentivisation of further reforms to improve and strengthen Samoa’s social protection system with the completion of two key legislative reforms in 2023–24: the National Provident Fund Amendment Act 2024 and National Digital Identification Act 2024. The National Provident Fund Amendment Act institutionalises the disability benefit as part of Samoa’s social protection systems, improving efficiency in the disbursement of disability funds to an estimated 2,300 beneficiaries. The National Digital Identification Act provides the legal framework for every Samoan citizen and resident to be issued with a unique identification, improving government efficiency and transparency in reaching vulnerable populations with targeted social protection benefits and disaster response initiatives.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia’s budget support incentivised and improved efficiency and delivery of targeted social protection benefits for Samoan citizens (including during disasters) through the progression of work towards a National Digital Identity. The regulations for the National Digital ID Act were approved by Cabinet in March 2025, which completed a policy action under the Joint Policy Action Matrix (JPAM) and acted as a disbursement trigger for the multi-donor budget support program. The Regulation was progressed with support of Australian-funded advisers in collaboration with the World Bank.
